name: Local SEO Lesson - GMB Location and Direction Manipulation (CTR)
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
Argues that where a GBP is registered largely decides how it ranks for competitive city terms, then describes ways to inflate "direction" requests.

# Key concepts
- In competitive niches, the map pack clusters around what Google treats as the city center. A listing in an outer suburb struggles for "[service] [city]".
- To find the "center", search the target term and note where the pack results sit on the map.
- Direction manipulation methods listed (the author calls them gray hat at best): requesting directions yourself and driving there, asking friends, paid software, or paying people on gig sites.

# TAG caution
TAG caution: this lesson includes tactics that violate Google Business Profile or review policies. They can get a listing suspended and are not used on TAG clients. Fake engagement is a policy risk and can waste budget.

# How this applies to TAG clients
- The location insight is useful for expectations: a client far from a city's center may need strong city pages and reviews to compete there (for example Pipeliners targets across the Phoenix metro, Alphalete in Colorado Springs).
- Use real heatmap or grid rank tracking (TAG uses [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas) local grids) to show clients where they are and are not visible.
